## Wave 4 Summary

Wave 4 attacks the rank-9b live edge of the fermion-mass / particle sector — the part of the spectrum the framework has NOT yet forced. Five of the six gates push a structural FAIL or compare-to-self result from S99–S101 toward a DERIVED resolution: (15) the per-generation quark kernel that supplies the gen-1 up/down crossing W2-4 proved impossible for uniform-κ; (16) a first-principles κ_ν replacing the back-solved s_ν target; (17) the scale-from-gap-eq / shape-from-ε_LX division of labor for the neutrino generation grading; (18) Model-C low-energy phenomenology on the W3-7 solved scales; (19) the substrate-canonical M₀-screening transfer convention that resolves the W4-5 CONVENTION-SENSITIVE ambiguity. The sixth gate (20) is a no-PDG-appeal m_H route-selection whose verdict KEYS the Wave-5 incumbent-BF 3-state refresh (cross-wave output contract, §"Wave 4 → Wave 5 Decision Point").

The wave is COMPUTE-class throughout. The governing structure is the same across every gate: physical fermion masses and the Higgs mass are spectral moments / dressed-block eigenvalues of D_K on Jensen-deformed SU(3); the "content" lives in SPLITTINGS, RATIOS, and SLOPE structure (per-generation κ_g, the (c²−v²) gradient, the a₄/a₂ moment ratio), not in absolute eigenvalues 14 OOM above the physical scales. Every numerical pin sources substrate-first; the m_H routes, quark anchors, κ_ν chain, Model-C scales, and §VII.BL ceiling are all knowledge-MCP-verified at plan-freeze (queries logged in §"Wave 4 Input-SHA Ledger").

## Wave 4 Decision Point Prerequisites

All six gates consume S101 (prior-session) artifacts that are LANDED on disk (SHAs in the Input-SHA Ledger). No item in Wave 4 depends on an UNMET S102 in-session upstream verdict; the wave is dispatchable from a cold start once S101 is closed.

- **Items 15–20** consume S101 W2/W3/W4 npz artifacts (all verified present, §"Input-SHA Ledger").
- **Item 20** (`S102-MH-ROUTE-SELECTION`) is the ONLY gate whose verdict propagates OUT of this wave: Wave-5 item 23 (`CF-S102-BF-SPINE-VS-LCDM`) consumes it via the pre-registered 3-state map (§"Wave 4 → Wave 5 Decision Point"). Item 20 has NO Wave-4-internal dependency — it can run in parallel with 15–19.
- No prereq is unmet at dispatch; therefore no gate in this wave is expected to honestly-close per `.claude/rules/mechanical-closure-discipline.md`. If an S101 npz fails its SHA pin at runtime, the consuming gate routes to PRE-REG-INC (machinery-input drift), NOT FAIL.

Within Wave 4 all six gates are independent and dispatch in parallel.

## §W4-15. CF-S102-QUARK-PERGEN-KERNEL

```yaml
# ---- Identity ----
gate_id: "CF-S102-QUARK-PERGEN-KERNEL"
schema_version: "R3"
trigger: "[SIGN]"
classification: "PARTICLE"
agent_type: "paasch-mass-quantization-analyst"
hypothesis: >
  A generation-DEPENDENT slope structure (per-generation kappa_g, or a
  non-monotone omega_g in C_2) DERIVED from the substrate dressed-block
  structure reproduces the gen-1 up/down inversion (m_u/m_d < 1) AND the
  gen-3 upright ordering (m_t/m_b > 1) simultaneously — which W2-4 proved
  impossible for ANY single (kappa_up, kappa_down) pair on a C_2-monotone
  omega-ladder — with per-component CKM framed as the misalignment of two
  rank-one dressings, the [SIGN] anchor preserved, and the W3-9 walls +
  [J,D_K]=0 intact.

method:

    Load the S101 W3 quark component-orientation ladders (D/c ladders, omega_g
    {0.253, 0.570, 1.140}, Omega^D/Omega^c = 2 exact). Construct a
    substrate-DERIVED per-generation kernel: either (route a) a per-generation
    kappa_g read off the dressed-block off-diagonal w_g vs diagonal d_g
    asymmetry, or (route b) a non-monotone omega_g(C_2) admitted by the
    Jensen-deformed sector geometry. Test the crossing condition (m_u/m_d < 1
    AND m_t/m_b > 1) on the DERIVED kernel against the PDG held-out ratios
    (m_u/m_d = 0.4596 gen-1; m_t/m_b = 41.28 gen-3 — held out, NOT fitted).
    Build per-component V_CKM = U_up^dagger U_down from the two frozen-block
    eigenbases (S99 structure) and verify the misalignment reproduces the
    Cabibbo-dominant texture. Selection-rule pre-flight (triality CG-admissibility)
    on every claimed nonzero inter-sector matrix element of the dressing.
  producing_script: "computations/_shared/s102_quark_pergen_kernel.py"

# ---- PRDR Checklist (8 items) ----
operator:
  type: "set"  # joint two-condition crossing test on a DERIVED kernel
  form: >
    PASS predicate = (m_u/m_d)_pred < 1  AND  (m_t/m_b)_pred > 1
    on the substrate-DERIVED per-gen kernel, with sign(SIGN-anchor) preserved
    AND triality-CG-admissibility(every nonzero inter-sector element) = True.

strict_PASS_boundary:
  value: >
    Joint crossing: (m_u/m_d)_pred < 1 (DERIVED) AND (m_t/m_b)_pred > 1 (DERIVED);
    PDG held-out anchors m_u/m_d = 0.4596, m_t/m_b = 41.28 reproduced to

boundary_reachable_analytically:

  proof_ref: >
    W2-4 impossibility theorem (uniform-kappa on C_2-monotone ladder cannot
    cross) is the analytic boundary; the per-gen kernel must lie OUTSIDE the
    uniform-kappa locus. The crossing-condition substitution chain (below)
    derives the sign requirement analytically.

reachable_rationals:
  includes_integer_mesh: false
  mesh_density: "continuous"  # kappa_g / omega_g are continuous slope params; the crossing boundary is a codim-1 surface in (kappa_1, kappa_3) space

machinery_pin_map:
  N_eval: "3"               # three generations
  L_max: "10"               # Peter-Weyl band for the dressed-block construction (canonical cache truncation)
  scan_range: "N/A — kernel DERIVED, not scanned (a free-scan would be load-and-compare-to-self per PRU Class 4)"
  step_size: "N/A — deterministic kernel construction"
  tolerance: "0.30"         # RATIO tol on held-out PDG ratios (DERIVED-not-fitted band)
  scheme: "FW"
  convention: "RATIO"       # per-generation mass RATIOS (intra-sector); the W0-9 RATIO class
  random_seed: "N/A — deterministic"
  GPU_path: "numpy.linalg"  # 2x2 frozen-block eigendecompositions per generation; tiny, CPU
  publication_precision: "4"  # crossing ratios published to 4 sig figs (consistency-check anchors)

audit_discriminators:
  audit_sha256_inputs: ["script", "canonical", "pinmap", "s101_w3_quark_component_orientation.npz"]
  content_sha256_inputs: ["script"]

substitution_chain:
  required: true
  content: |
    Claim: "A per-generation kappa_g (non-uniform across C_2) is REQUIRED to
            produce gen-1 inversion (m_u/m_d < 1) AND gen-3 upright (m_t/m_b > 1);
            a single uniform (kappa_up, kappa_down) pair CANNOT."

    Step 1 — Definitions [cite s101_w3_quark_component_orientation.npz + S99 frozen-block]:
      For sector S in {up, down}, generation g, the dressed 2x2 block is
        B_g^S = [[ d_g^S , w_g^S ],[ conj(w_g^S) , d_g^S ]]
      with diagonal d_g^S the bare ladder entry and off-diagonal w_g^S the dressing.
      The physical mass eigenvalues are
        m_{g,pm}^S = d_g^S +/- |w_g^S|.
      The per-generation RATIO observable is
        r_g = m_g^{up} / m_g^{down}   (the heavier eigenvalue of each sector).
      The dressing magnitude is parametrized
        |w_g^S| = kappa_g^S * f(C_2(g))    [kappa_g^S = per-gen slope; f = C_2 form factor]
      where C_2(g) is the quadratic Casimir of generation g's sector irrep,
      C_2 monotone-increasing in g (omega_g {0.253, 0.570, 1.140} from the npz).

    Step 2 — Substitution (crossing condition, no simplification):
      Gen-1 inversion requires r_1 < 1:
        ( d_1^{up} + kappa_1^{up} f(C_2(1)) ) / ( d_1^{down} + kappa_1^{down} f(C_2(1)) ) < 1
      Gen-3 upright requires r_3 > 1:
        ( d_3^{up} + kappa_3^{up} f(C_2(3)) ) / ( d_3^{down} + kappa_3^{down} f(C_2(3)) ) > 1

    Step 3 — Simplification (uniform-kappa case: kappa_g^S = kappa^S for all g):
      Under uniform kappa, both inequalities share the SAME kappa^up, kappa^down.
      Gen-1: d_1^{up} + kappa^{up} f_1 < d_1^{down} + kappa^{down} f_1
           => (kappa^{up} - kappa^{down}) f_1 < d_1^{down} - d_1^{up}
      Gen-3: (kappa^{up} - kappa^{down}) f_3 > d_3^{down} - d_3^{up}
      With f_3 > f_1 > 0 (C_2 monotone) and (d^{down} - d^{up}) of fixed sign,
      the two inequalities impose OPPOSITE-SIGN constraints on the SAME scalar
      (kappa^{up} - kappa^{down}) unless the bare-gap term flips sign across
      generations — which the C_2-monotone bare ladder does NOT do (W2-4 result).
      => no uniform (kappa^{up}, kappa^{down}) satisfies both. [W2-4 reproduced]

    Step 4 — Canonical form (per-gen kernel):
      Allowing kappa_g^S to depend on g, the two inequalities become INDEPENDENT
      in (kappa_1^S) and (kappa_3^S):
        (kappa_1^{up} - kappa_1^{down}) f_1 < d_1^{down} - d_1^{up}    [gen-1 free]
        (kappa_3^{up} - kappa_3^{down}) f_3 > d_3^{down} - d_3^{up}    [gen-3 free]
      The crossing is REACHABLE iff the substrate supplies kappa_g^S with the
      required per-gen sign pattern:
        sign(kappa_1^{up} - kappa_1^{down}) = -sign(d_1^{down} - d_1^{up}) admissible
        sign(kappa_3^{up} - kappa_3^{down}) = +sign(d_3^{down} - d_3^{up}) admissible

    Step 5 — Direction read-off:
      The crossing condition is SATISFIABLE only by a kernel whose per-gen slope
      asymmetry (kappa_g^{up} - kappa_g^{down}) CHANGES SIGN between g=1 and g=3
      (or is non-monotone in C_2). The gate PASSes iff the substrate-DERIVED
      kernel exhibits this sign change FROM FIRST PRINCIPLES (the dressed-block
      w_g asymmetry), NOT by fitting kappa_g to PDG.

    Conclusion: PASS requires a DERIVED per-gen kernel with sign-changing
      slope asymmetry; uniform-kappa is analytically excluded (W2-4).

    --- Selection-rule pre-flight (triality CG-admissibility) ---
    For any claimed nonzero inter-sector matrix element <psi_a | O_dressing | psi_b>
    between SU(3) irrep sectors a, b with the dressing operator O:
      t(p,q) = (p - q) mod 3  [center character].
      Admissibility: t(a) == t(b) + t(O) (mod 3); necessary condition.
      A squared-modulus dressing |w|^2 carries t(O) = 0 ALWAYS; a linear
      dressing w carries the center character of its representation content.
      Any inter-sector element failing t(a) == t(b) + t(O) (mod 3) is EXACTLY
      zero and MUST NOT be counted as a CKM misalignment channel.
      [landed S101 W8b-1; math-scripts.md §"Selection-rule pre-flight"]
```

## §W4-16. CF-S102-KAPPA-NU-FIRSTPRINCIPLES

```yaml

hypothesis: >
  The greybody construction on the s84 B-branch spectrum FORCES the
  Dirac-neutrino shape slope kappa_nu (hence s_nu = +0.5469) from the sector
  (c^2 - v^2) gradient ALONE — derived INDEPENDENTLY of the S99 Y-ratios that
  W3-3 back-solved against — with the sign-flip preserved; this closes whether
  s_nu = +0.5469 is FORCED (currently consistent-but-not-forced / compare-to-self).

method:
  description: >
    Load the S101 kappa_nu greybody data (kappa_nu,bare = 11.4877 M_KK,
    B_nu = -0.1453, domega/dC_2 = -3.764). Re-derive kappa_nu from the
    Dirac-neutrino-channel (c^2 - v^2) gradient on the s84 B-branch spectrum
    (full-confidence post-L4) WITHOUT importing the S99 Y-ratio targets.
    The Kitaev exit-rate anchor 2*pi*T(a_4) = kappa_exit fixes the greybody
    normalization from substrate spectral data. Compute s_nu^pred = +/- sign *
    |slope| and compare to the pre-declared +0.546948 (II.3 sign-flip corner,
    g = C_2, q -> 0+). NO back-solve: the target value MUST NOT appear in the
    derivation path; the script asserts (via a guard) that the +0.546948 anchor
    is loaded ONLY for the final comparison, never as an input to kappa_nu.
  producing_script: "computations/_shared/s102_kappa_nu_firstprinciples.py"

# ---- PRDR Checklist (8 items) ----
operator:
  type: "ratio"
  form: "|s_nu^pred - s_nu^target| / |s_nu^target| <= tau   (s_nu^target = +0.546948)"

strict_PASS_boundary:
  value: "0.01"   # RATIO tol 1% on the shape slope s_nu
  direction: "<="

boundary_reachable_analytically:
  bool: true
  proof_ref: >
    The Kitaev exit-rate 2*pi*T(a_4) = kappa_exit and the (c^2 - v^2) gradient
    sign on the B-branch are both closed-form on the s84 spectrum; the slope
    magnitude follows by the greybody transmission integral. Sign-flip chain below.

reachable_rationals:
  includes_integer_mesh: false
  mesh_density: "continuous"  # s_nu is a continuous slope; the target +0.546948 is a single point

machinery_pin_map:
  N_eval: "<count of s84 B-branch eigenvalues entering the (c^2-v^2) gradient — pinned at runtime from the s84 cache, NOT free>"
  L_max: "10"               # s84 B-branch canonical truncation (post-L4 full-confidence)
  scan_range: "N/A — kappa_nu DERIVED from the gradient, not scanned"
  step_size: "N/A — deterministic"
  tolerance: "0.01"         # RATIO 1% on s_nu
  scheme: "FW"
  convention: "ABSOLUTE"    # s_nu is an ABSOLUTE shape-slope value (a signed magnitude), not an intra-family ratio
  random_seed: "N/A — deterministic"
  GPU_path: "torch.linalg"  # s84 B-branch spectrum >= 100x100 per-block; GPU eigvals per math-scripts.md
  publication_precision: "4"  # s_nu published to 4 sig figs (+0.5469)

audit_discriminators:
  audit_sha256_inputs: ["script", "canonical", "pinmap", "s101_kappa_nu_greybody.npz"]
  content_sha256_inputs: ["script"]

substitution_chain:
  required: true
  content: |
    Claim: "The sign of the Dirac-neutrino greybody response is FIXED by the
            substrate sign chain to +0.5469 (a WIDENING / positive slope), and
            this sign is independent of the S99 Y-ratio back-solve."

    Step 1 — Definitions [cite session-84-s5-connes-cohomology-synthesis + s101_kappa_nu_greybody.npz]:
      The greybody-response sign of the neutrino-channel shape slope is
        sign(gv_response) = sign(e^{-tau_fold}) * sign(Vol_{SU(3)}) * sign(J_C2) * sign(kernel)
      with the canonical kernel-sign convention sign(kernel) = (-1) [S84-s5].
      B_nu = -0.1453 (the bare greybody coefficient; s101 npz).
      domega/dC_2 = -3.764 (the C_2-gradient of the sector frequency; s101 npz).
      The Kitaev exit anchor: 2*pi*T(a_4) = kappa_exit fixes the magnitude scale.

    Step 2 — Substitution (no simplification):
      sign(gv_response) = sign(e^{-tau_fold}) * sign(Vol_{SU(3)}) * sign(J_C2) * (-1)
      With e^{-tau_fold} > 0 (tau_fold = 0.190 real) => sign(e^{-tau_fold}) = +1,
      Vol_{SU(3)} > 0 => sign(Vol_{SU(3)}) = +1.

    Step 3 — Simplification (one factor per line):
      = (+1) * (+1) * sign(J_C2) * (-1)
      = -sign(J_C2)
      The sign of J_C2 (the C_2-Jacobian of the gv-stencil) is read off the
      B-branch (c^2 - v^2) gradient: on the B-branch, the (c^2 - v^2) gradient
      and domega/dC_2 = -3.764 < 0 give sign(J_C2) = -1.

    Step 4 — Canonical form:
      sign(gv_response) = -sign(J_C2) = -(-1) = +1.
      => s_nu^pred > 0  (POSITIVE slope = a WIDENING of the shape).

    Step 5 — Direction read-off:
      The substrate sign chain FORCES s_nu^pred = +|slope| (a sign-flip TO
      positive / widening), independent of the S99 Y-ratios. PASS requires the
      DERIVED magnitude |s_nu^pred| match +0.546948 to RATIO 1%, with the
      derivation path containing NO reference to the Y-ratio targets (back-solve
      guard). The sign-flip (widening) is the SIGN-verdict; the magnitude match
      is the MAGNITUDE-verdict.

    Conclusion: sign-flip to +0.5469 is substrate-FORCED; PASS iff the
      Y-ratio-independent magnitude lands within 1%.
```

```yaml
                      = h(C_2(3)) / h(C_2(2))
```

## §W4-18. CF-S102-MODELC-PHENO-SCALES

```yaml
# ---- Identity ----
gate_id: "CF-S102-MODELC-PHENO-SCALES"
schema_version: "R3"
trigger: "[VERIFY]"
classification: "PARTICLE"
agent_type: "paasch-mass-quantization-analyst"
hypothesis: >
  The Model-C (Pati-Salam G422D) 0-free-parameter ordered solution on the W3-7
  solved scales — M_C = 5.08e13 GeV (leptoquark S_1) and M_U = 7.68e14 GeV
  (unification / proton-decay-adjacent) — SURVIVES current experimental bounds:
  the proton-lifetime bound at M_U (Super-K / Hyper-K) AND the leptoquark S_1
  flavor bounds at M_C.

method:
  description: >
    Load the S101 PS-RGE Model-C solution (M_C = 5.08e13 GeV, M_U = 7.68e14 GeV,
    alpha_U^{-1} = 39.47, the three coupling trajectories). Compute the
    framework proton lifetime tau_p ~ M_U^4 / (alpha_U^2 m_p^5) from the SOLVED
    M_U (NOT the generic M_KK estimate) and compare to the current Super-K bound
    (tau_p(p->e+ pi0) > 2.4e34 yr, 2023) and the Hyper-K projected reach
    (~10^35 yr at Yr-10). Compute the leptoquark S_1 contributions to flavor
    observables (the strongest current constraint at M_C = 5.08e13 GeV — note
    M_C is far above direct-search reach, so the binding constraints are
    loop-level flavor: e.g. K-Kbar / proton-decay-adjacent rare processes) and
    compare to current flavor bounds. PASS = both survive; FAIL = either scale
    is experimentally excluded (the falsifier-rigor companion).
  producing_script: "computations/_shared/s102_modelc_pheno_scales.py"

# ---- PRDR Checklist (8 items) ----
operator:
  type: "set"   # two-condition survival test (proton-lifetime bound AND leptoquark flavor bound)
  form: >
    PASS = (tau_p^pred(M_U) > tau_p^bound_SuperK)  AND
           (leptoquark S_1 flavor amplitude at M_C < current flavor bound)

strict_PASS_boundary:
  value: >
    tau_p^pred(M_U=7.68e14) > 2.4e34 yr (Super-K p->e+pi0, 2023 bound) AND
    S_1 leptoquark loop amplitude at M_C=5.08e13 below the binding flavor bound
    (operationalized in-script from the dominant rare process).
  direction: "set-membership (both survival inequalities hold)"

boundary_reachable_analytically:
  bool: true
  proof_ref: >
    tau_p ~ M_U^4 / (alpha_U^2 m_p^5) is the dimensional GUT proton-decay
    estimate (atlas-05 Window-17; falsifier-watchlist proton_lifetime row); the
    M_U, alpha_U^{-1} are the S101 W3-7 RGE-solved values (0 free params).
    Leptoquark S_1 flavor amplitudes scale as 1/M_C^2 (4-fermion EFT).

reachable_rationals:
  includes_integer_mesh: false
  mesh_density: "continuous"  # tau_p and flavor amplitudes are continuous; the bounds are fixed experimental thresholds

machinery_pin_map:
  N_eval: "1"               # single-point evaluation at the solved (M_C, M_U) scales (no scan; the scales are 0-free-param SOLVED)
  L_max: "N/A — RGE/EFT computation, not a Peter-Weyl truncation"
  scan_range: "N/A — scales SOLVED (load-and-evaluate, NOT load-and-compare-to-self: the bounds are independent experimental data)"
  step_size: "N/A — deterministic"
  tolerance: "N/A — survival test against experimental bounds (inequality, not a tolerance band)"
  scheme: "MS"             # MS-bar running couplings (the RGE scheme of the S101 PS solution)
  convention: "ABSOLUTE"   # tau_p is an absolute lifetime; flavor amplitudes absolute
  random_seed: "N/A — deterministic"
  GPU_path: "numpy.linalg" # RGE/EFT arithmetic; CPU
  publication_precision: "3"  # tau_p^pred published to 3 sig figs

audit_discriminators:
  audit_sha256_inputs: ["script", "canonical", "pinmap", "s101_ps_rge_modelc_sin2_mz.npz"]
  content_sha256_inputs: ["script"]

substitution_chain:
  required: true
  content: |
    Claim: "The Model-C solved unification scale M_U = 7.68e14 GeV yields a
            proton lifetime ABOVE the current Super-K bound (survives) — the
            direction (predicted > bound) must be checked, not assumed."

    Step 1 — Definitions [cite s101_ps_rge_modelc_sin2_mz.npz + atlas-05 Window-17]:
      M_U = 7.68e14 GeV (S101 W3-7 RGE-solved Model-C unification scale).
      alpha_U^{-1} = 39.47 => alpha_U = 1/39.47 = 0.02534.
      m_p = 0.938272 GeV (proton mass).
      tau_p ~ M_U^4 / (alpha_U^2 * m_p^5)   [dimensional GUT estimate, p->e+pi0].
      Super-K bound (2023): tau_p^bound = 2.4e34 yr.

    Step 2 — Substitution (no simplification):
      tau_p^pred ~ (7.68e14)^4 / ( (0.02534)^2 * (0.938272)^5 )  [GeV^-1, then convert]

    Step 3 — Simplification (OOM read; in-script does the unit conversion exactly):
      (7.68e14)^4   = 3.48e59 GeV^4
      (0.02534)^2   = 6.42e-4
      (0.938272)^5  = 0.728 GeV^5
      tau_p^pred ~ 3.48e59 / (6.42e-4 * 0.728) GeV^-1 = 7.45e62 GeV^-1
      Convert: 1 GeV^-1 = 6.58e-25 s = 2.09e-32 yr
      tau_p^pred ~ 7.45e62 * 2.09e-32 yr ~ 1.6e31 * (O(1) coefficient) yr.
      NOTE: the dimensional estimate gives ~10^31-10^36 yr depending on the
      O(1) GUT coefficient (the model-dependent factor in-script must pin from
      the Model-C operator content); the DIRECTION test is tau_p^pred vs 2.4e34.

    Step 4 — Direction read-off:
      Whether tau_p^pred > 2.4e34 (SURVIVES) or < 2.4e34 (EXCLUDED) depends on
      the model-dependent O(1) coefficient computed in-script from the Model-C
      G422D operator content. The gate does NOT pre-assume survival; it computes
      the coefficient and reads off the direction. M_U = 7.68e14 is ~1.3 OOM
      BELOW the canonical 10^16 GUT scale (Window-17 tau_p ~10^36 at 10^16) =>
      tau_p^pred ~ (7.68e14/1e16)^4 * 10^36 ~ (0.0768)^4 * 10^36 ~ 3.5e31 yr
      naive => this is BELOW 2.4e34 => the survival is NOT automatic and the
      gate may FAIL (proton-decay-EXCLUDED) unless the Model-C operator
      structure suppresses the rate. This is the substantive risk the gate maps.

    Conclusion: the direction (survive vs exclude) is the gate output; the naive
      M_U^4 scaling FLAGS that M_U = 7.68e14 is low enough that proton-decay
      exclusion is a LIVE possibility — the gate is a genuine falsifier.

input_files:

    path: "computations/_shared/canonical_constants.py"
    sha256: "9f2fe9983ecbbb76a2ba1b3e951cf9275deda8d7f2241576ef23b7f728ba1047"
  ps_rge_modelc:

# ---- fb_pair ----

  backward: "the m_H / unification consistency surface; falsifier-master-inventory proton-lifetime row (mack sole-writer if a new value lands); any Model-C-vs-Model-other adjudication"

dual_prior:
  track_A: "0.6 — Model-C survives both bounds; the 0-free-param solution is experimentally viable"
  track_B: "0.4 — at least one scale is experimentally excluded (M_U = 7.68e14 is low for proton decay; this is the live falsifier risk per Step 3-4)"
  discriminator: "PASS -> 0.9 to Track A (both survive); FAIL -> 0.9 to Track B (Model-C excluded by current bounds — the falsifier fires)"

# ---- Output artifacts ----
output_artifacts:
  script:
    path: "computations/session-102/s102_modelc_pheno_scales.py"
    artifact_kind: "script"
    must_contain:
      - "from canonical_constants import"
      - "print_verdict_payload"
  data:
    path: "computations/session-102/s102_modelc_pheno_scales.npz"
    artifact_kind: "data"
    optional: false

    path: "computations/session-102/s102_modelc_pheno_scales.png"
    artifact_kind: "plot"

    artifact_kind: "verdict_line"

# ---- Verdict rubric ----
PASS_meaning: >
  Model-C survives BOTH the proton-lifetime bound at M_U (Super-K/Hyper-K) AND
  the leptoquark S_1 flavor bounds at M_C. The 0-free-parameter ordered solution
```

## §W4-19. CF-S102-M0-TRANSFER-CONVENTION

```yaml
# ---- Identity ----

  (-11/670 = -1.642%) — resolving the ~1.2% ambiguity that W4-5 left

  tolerance), with the band-shrink DIRECTION (the screening lowers the residual
  toward PDG; sign = PASS) preserved.

method:
  description: >
    Load the S101 W4 M_0 BCS-screening data (r_KK^scr, r_KK^scr,RG,
    delta_solve = 0.267). The M_0-screening transfer factor maps the unscreened
    KK residual to the screened residual; two conventions exist: (PRIM)
    m_H-level first-power -11/670 = -1.642%, and (RG) boundary-level RG
    -0.461%. DERIVE which transfer level is the substrate-canonical one from the
    BCS machinery (S62): is the screening applied at the BOUNDARY (RG running of
    the condensate) or at the m_H LEVEL (first-power correction to the physical
    Higgs mass)? The derivation rests on WHERE in the BCS gap-to-mass chain the
    Volovik-partition effacement screening enters. PASS iff the convention is

  producing_script: "computations/_shared/s102_m0_transfer_convention.py"

# ---- PRDR Checklist (8 items) ----
operator:
  type: "ratio"
  form: >
    PASS = convention DERIVED (boundary-RG OR m_H-first-power selected from BCS
    chain position) AND |r_PRIM - r_RG|_under_derived_convention <= 0.010
    AND sign(screening correction) = negative (band-shrink toward PDG).

strict_PASS_boundary:

boundary_reachable_analytically:

    boundary-RG = -0.461% (S101 W4-5). The derivation is WHERE the BCS effacement
    screening enters the gap-to-mass chain (S62 BCS machinery); the chain
    position is analytically determined by the Volovik-partition structure.

reachable_rationals:
  includes_integer_mesh: true
  mesh_density: "2 — the two candidate conventions (-11/670 and -0.461%) are the discrete admissible set; the derivation selects one"

machinery_pin_map:
  N_eval: "2"               # two candidate transfer conventions
  L_max: "N/A — BCS gap-to-mass chain, not a Peter-Weyl truncation"
  scan_range: "N/A — convention DERIVED (chain-position argument), not scanned"
  step_size: "N/A — deterministic"
  tolerance: "0.010"        # 1.0% spread under the derived convention
  scheme: "SA"             # spectral-action / BCS gap machinery (S62)
  convention: "MIXED"      # the gate DERIVES the convention — both candidate transfer levels are in scope until the derivation selects
  random_seed: "N/A — deterministic"
  GPU_path: "numpy.linalg" # BCS gap-to-mass arithmetic; CPU
  publication_precision: "4"  # the screening correction published to 4 sig figs
  CLASS: "FULL"            # the BCS machinery is FULL physical (S62 gap equation), NOT a SCHEMATIC helper

audit_discriminators:
  audit_sha256_inputs: ["script", "canonical", "pinmap", "s101_w4_m0_bcs_screening.npz"]
  content_sha256_inputs: ["script"]

substitution_chain:
  required: true
  content: |
    Claim: "The M_0-screening LOWERS the m_H residual toward PDG (the band-shrink
            direction: the screened residual is SMALLER in magnitude than the
            unscreened residual; sign = PASS), regardless of which transfer
            convention is canonical."

    Step 1 — Definitions [cite s101_w4_m0_bcs_screening.npz + S62 BCS + A10 tree m_H=134]:
      r_KK = unscreened KK residual = m_H^KK/m_H_obs - 1 = 131.8/125.1 - 1 = +5.356%.
      (also r_tree = 134/125.1 - 1 = +7.114% for the tree route.)
      Screening corrections (two conventions):
        delta_RG   = -0.461%   (boundary-level RG transfer)
        delta_PRIM = -11/670 = -1.642%   (m_H-level first-power transfer)
      Screened residual: r_scr = r_KK + delta.
      delta_solve = 0.267 (the BCS solve discriminant; s101 npz).

    Step 2 — Substitution (band-shrink direction, no simplification):
      |r_scr| < |r_KK|  iff  the screening MOVES the residual toward zero, i.e.
      delta has OPPOSITE sign to r_KK and |delta| < 2|r_KK|.
      r_KK = +5.356% > 0.

    Step 3 — Simplification (both conventions):
      delta_RG   = -0.461% < 0  => opposite sign to r_KK; |delta_RG| = 0.461% < 2*5.356%
        => |r_scr,RG| = |5.356 - 0.461|% = 4.895% < 5.356% = |r_KK|. [SHRINKS]
      delta_PRIM = -1.642% < 0  => opposite sign to r_KK; |delta_PRIM| = 1.642% < 2*5.356%
        => |r_scr,PRIM| = |5.356 - 1.642|% = 3.714% < 5.356% = |r_KK|. [SHRINKS]

    Step 4 — Canonical form (the ambiguity):
      Spread between conventions = |delta_PRIM - delta_RG| = |1.642 - 0.461|% = 1.181%.
      1.181% > 1.0% tolerance => CONVENTION-SENSITIVE (W4-5 result).
      The DERIVATION must select ONE convention from the BCS-chain position of
      the Volovik effacement screening:
        - if screening enters at the CONDENSATE BOUNDARY (RG running of the gap)
          => boundary-RG convention (-0.461%).
        - if screening enters at the PHYSICAL m_H (first-power correction to the
          pole mass) => m_H-first-power convention (-1.642%).
      The chain position is fixed by WHERE the Volovik partition acts: the
      effacement Gamma_eff = 0.99970 screens the VACUUM partition (a boundary
      quantity), which argues for the BOUNDARY-RG level.

    Step 5 — Direction read-off:
      SIGN-verdict: both conventions shrink the band (delta < 0, opposite to
      r_KK > 0) => the band-shrink DIRECTION is PASS regardless of convention.
      MAGNITUDE-verdict: PASS iff the DERIVED convention collapses the spread to
      <= 1.0% (i.e. the derivation eliminates the ambiguity by selecting one
      transfer level), FAIL if both remain admissible (spread stays 1.181%).

    Conclusion: band-shrink sign = PASS (forced); the gate's substantive output
      is whether the BCS-chain-position argument DERIVES a unique convention.

input_files:
  canonical_constants:
    path: "computations/_shared/canonical_constants.py"
    sha256: "9f2fe9983ecbbb76a2ba1b3e951cf9275deda8d7f2241576ef23b7f728ba1047"
  m0_bcs_screening:
    path: "computations/session-101/s101_w4_m0_bcs_screening.npz"
    sha256: "46ff62edcc3fa6a943cfea54f9aeca311333a4a0334e0a55e6fe5474d660f2b2"

# ---- fb_pair ----
fb_pair:
  forward: "s101_w4_m0_bcs_screening (r_KK^scr, r_KK^scr,RG, delta_solve=0.267; audit 1a1eff66); S62 BCS machinery (THRESHOLD-62); A10 tree m_H=134; Gamma_effacement=0.99970"
  backward: "S102-MH-ROUTE-SELECTION (item 20) — the screening level feeds the m_H route residuals; the m_H route 3-state to Wave-5"

dual_prior:
  track_A: "0.5 — the BCS-chain position DERIVES a unique transfer convention (boundary-RG, per the Volovik-partition-screens-the-boundary argument), collapsing the spread <= 1.0%"
  track_B: "0.5 — both transfer levels remain admissible from the BCS chain; the convention is genuinely ambiguous and routes to a workshop"
  discriminator: "PASS -> 0.9 to Track A (convention derived, spread collapsed); INFO -> 0.9 to Track B (needs a 2-agent workshop on the BCS-chain position); FAIL -> the band-shrink sign itself inverts (deeper BCS problem)"

# ---- Output artifacts ----
output_artifacts:
  script:
    path: "computations/session-102/s102_m0_transfer_convention.py"
    artifact_kind: "script"
    must_contain:
      - "from canonical_constants import"
      - "print_verdict_payload"
  data:
    path: "computations/session-102/s102_m0_transfer_convention.npz"
    artifact_kind: "data"
    optional: false
  plot:
    path: "computations/session-102/s102_m0_transfer_convention.png"
    artifact_kind: "plot"
    optional: false
  verdict_line:
    path: "computations/session-102/s102_gate_verdicts.txt"
    artifact_kind: "verdict_line"
    must_contain: "^CF-S102-M0-TRANSFER-CONVENTION:.* audit_sha256=[a-f0-9]{64}"
    companion_row_required: true
    schema_v2_3tuple_required: true   # [SIGN] trigger — band-shrink-direction 3-tuple REQUIRED
  wp_section:
    path: "sessions/session-102/session-102-w4-workingpaper.md"

      - "\\*\\*Verdict\\*\\*:.*(PASS|FAIL|INFO)"
      - "\\*\\*Output Artifacts\\*\\*"
      - "\\*\\*MCP Pre-Compute Audit\\*\\*"

# ---- Verdict rubric ----
PASS_meaning: >
  The substrate-canonical M_0-screening transfer convention is DERIVED from the

substrate_framing: |
```

## §W4-20. S102-MH-ROUTE-SELECTION

```yaml
# ---- Identity ----
gate_id: "S102-MH-ROUTE-SELECTION"
schema_version: "R3"
trigger: "[CHAIN]"
classification: "PARTICLE"
agent_type: "phonon-first-cosmologist"   # a_4-moment derivation owner (per BF-spine workshop); cross-checked by connes-ncg-theorist
hypothesis: >
  The a_4-moment KK-threshold structure of the transverse |S|^2 fiber-embedding
  mode FORCES a UNIQUE intra-KK-family m_H route — KK-L5 (127.5) vs KK-threshold
  (131.8) — via a selection criterion writable WITHOUT citing which route lands
  nearest PDG 125.25 (no-PDG-appeal); if no unique route is forced, the verdict
  is FAIL-ACCOMMODATION (best-fit selection).

method:
  description: >
    The two intra-KK-family m_H routes are KK-L5 (Aitken-Gaussian Delta^2 of the
    L=4,5,6 KK-threshold series, edge 127.5, S_4 = 1.14290915 from
    s66_kk_threshold_l5_results.txt) and KK-threshold (131.8, the converged
    a_4-moment KK-threshold correction, m_H_FW_KK_threshold). The zeta route
    (138.5, HIGGS-ZETA-67) is already EXCLUDED (zeta-regulated, not the physical
    regularization). The mu_BC route (188.19 / ACCOMMODATION-flagged) is the
    best-fit surface. DERIVE the selection criterion from the a_4^{regulator}-tagged
    KK-threshold moment structure: which route is the substrate-FORCED convergent
    limit of the a_4-moment KK-threshold correction to the |S|^2 mode? The
    criterion (e.g. whether the Aitken-accelerated edge or the directly-converged
    moment is the canonical a_4 KK-threshold value) MUST be statable and
    evaluable WITHOUT loading m_H_obs = 125.25 — the script asserts (back-solve
    guard) that m_H_obs is loaded ONLY for the final reporting comparison, never
    as a selection input. PASS = a unique route forced by the a_4 structure;
    FAIL-ACCOMMODATION = the criterion does not discriminate and the route is
    chosen by proximity to PDG.
  producing_script: "computations/_shared/s102_mh_route_selection.py"

# ---- PRDR Checklist (8 items) ----
operator:
  type: "set"   # two-branch adjudication: {FORCED unique route} vs {NO forced route / ACCOMMODATION}
  form: >
    PASS = the a_4^{regulator}-tagged KK-threshold structure forces a UNIQUE
    route in {KK-L5(127.5), KK-threshold(131.8)} via a no-PDG-appeal criterion.
    FAIL-ACCOMMODATION = criterion does not discriminate (route chosen by
    proximity to PDG 125.25).

strict_PASS_boundary:
  value: >
    UNIQUE-route-forced by the a_4-moment selection criterion, evaluated with
    m_H_obs ABSENT from the selection path (back-solve guard asserts m_H_obs not
    in the criterion's input set). This is a set-membership / adjudication
    boundary, NOT a numerical tolerance.
  direction: "set-membership (criterion selects exactly one route, no PDG appeal)"

boundary_reachable_analytically:
  bool: true
  proof_ref: >
    The a_4-moment KK-threshold structure (a_4_FW_zeta = 1350.7216, the
    Yang-Mills + Higgs-quartic fourth Seeley-DeWitt moment) and the KK-L5
    Aitken-Gaussian acceleration (S_4 = 1.14290915 from s66) are both closed-form;
    the selection criterion is whether the directly-converged a_4 KK-threshold
    correction or the Aitken-extrapolated edge is the canonical convergent limit
    — an analytic property of the KK-series convergence, NOT a fit.

reachable_rationals:
  includes_integer_mesh: false
  mesh_density: "discrete-2 — the admissible route set is {KK-L5, KK-threshold} (zeta excluded, mu_BC is the ACCOMMODATION surface); the criterion selects within this discrete set"

machinery_pin_map:
  N_eval: "2"               # two intra-KK-family routes adjudicated (KK-L5, KK-threshold)
  L_max: "10"               # canonical Peter-Weyl truncation for the a_4-moment evaluation; KK-series uses L=4,5,6 for the Aitken-Gaussian
  scan_range: "N/A — route SELECTION, not a scan"
  step_size: "N/A — deterministic"
  tolerance: "N/A — adjudication (FORCED vs ACCOMMODATION), not a numerical band"
  scheme: "FW"
  convention: "ABSOLUTE"   # m_H route values are absolute GeV predictions
  random_seed: "N/A — deterministic"
  GPU_path: "torch.linalg" # a_4-moment KK-threshold structure on the D_K spectrum >= 100x100 per-block; GPU
  regulator_pin: "a_4^{ζ}"  # MANDATORY: the a_4-moment KK-threshold structure cites the zeta-regulated a_4 (a_4_FW_zeta, S75); regulator-pin-discipline.md
  publication_precision: "4"  # route values published to 4 sig figs (127.5, 131.8)

audit_discriminators:
  audit_sha256_inputs: ["script", "canonical", "pinmap"]
  content_sha256_inputs: ["script"]

substitution_chain:
  required: true
  content: |
    Claim: "A UNIQUE m_H route is selectable from the a_4-moment KK-threshold
            convergence structure WITHOUT appeal to which route lands nearest
            PDG — the selection criterion is an analytic property of the KK-series,
            not a proximity-to-data argument."

    Step 1 — Definitions [cite a_4_FW_zeta(S75) + s66_kk_threshold_l5_results.txt + m_H_FW_KK_threshold]:
      Route A (KK-L5): m_H^A = Aitken-Gaussian Delta^2 extrapolation of the
        L=4,5,6 KK-threshold series; the S-series is S_3=0.50347910, S_4=1.14290915
        (s66 output); the extrapolated edge maps to m_H^A ~ 127.5 GeV.
      Route B (KK-threshold): m_H^B = the directly-converged a_4-moment KK-threshold
        correction to the |S|^2 mode = 131.8 GeV (m_H_FW_KK_threshold; the
        a_4^{ζ} = 1350.7216 Yang-Mills + Higgs-quartic moment fixes the correction).
      EXCLUDED: m_H^zeta = 138.5 (HIGGS-ZETA-67; zeta-regulated, not physical reg).
      ACCOMMODATION surface: m_H^muBC = 188.19 (mu_BC bi-criterion fit; flagged).
      m_H_obs = 125.1 (PDG) — LOADED ONLY for final comparison (back-solve guard).

    Step 2 — Substitution (the selection criterion, no PDG):
      Define the criterion C(route) = "is this route the substrate-FORCED
      convergent limit of the a_4-moment KK-threshold correction?"
        - Route B is the DIRECT a_4-moment value: it is the converged correction
          computed from a_4^{ζ} at the canonical L_max with NO extrapolation.
        - Route A is an Aitken-ACCELERATED extrapolation of a truncated L=4,5,6
          series: it presupposes the bare series has NOT converged at L=6 and
          accelerates it.
      The criterion asks: does the a_4-moment KK-threshold series CONVERGE by
      the canonical L_max (=> Route B canonical, Aitken superfluous) or does it
      REQUIRE acceleration (=> Route A canonical, the direct value premature)?

    Step 3 — Simplification (analytic convergence test):
      The a_4-moment KK-threshold correction is governed by the Casimir-bounded
      KK-tower sum; its convergence rate is set by the Friedrich-Bar saturation
      of the new-sector eigenvalue floor (math-scripts.md §"D_K Block-Diagonality").
      If the bottom-K |S|^2 KK-threshold contribution is L_max-SATURATED at the
      canonical truncation, the DIRECT moment (Route B, 131.8) IS the converged
      limit and Aitken acceleration of a saturated series is spurious
      (Aitken on an already-converged series returns the same fixed point or
      over-corrects) => Route B forced.
      If the contribution is NOT saturated (the Aitken Delta^2 of L=4,5,6 differs
      materially from the L=10 direct value), the series needs acceleration =>
      Route A forced.

    Step 4 — Direction read-off (no PDG):
      The selection is FORCED by the convergence behavior of the a_4-moment
      KK-threshold series — a substrate-spectral property — NOT by |m_H^route -
      125.1|. The script computes the saturation diagnostic (direct L=10 a_4
      moment vs Aitken-Gaussian L=4,5,6 extrapolation) and reads off:
        - if |direct - Aitken| within the Friedrich-Bar saturation floor =>
          series converged => Route B (131.8) FORCED.
        - if |direct - Aitken| exceeds the floor => series needs acceleration =>
          Route A (127.5) FORCED.
      PASS = a unique route forced by this diagnostic. FAIL-ACCOMMODATION = the
      diagnostic is INCONCLUSIVE (both routes survive the convergence test) and
      the only remaining discriminator is proximity to PDG => the route is an
      ACCOMMODATION, not a prediction.

    Conclusion: the no-PDG-appeal criterion is the a_4-moment KK-series
      convergence/saturation diagnostic; PASS = unique route forced by it.

input_files:
  canonical_constants:
    path: "computations/_shared/canonical_constants.py"
    sha256: "9f2fe9983ecbbb76a2ba1b3e951cf9275deda8d7f2241576ef23b7f728ba1047"
  # The KK-L5 S-series (S_4=1.14290915) lives in s66_kk_threshold_l5_results.txt
  # (archive, S66); it is NOT yet a canonical constant. The producing script
  # MUST re-derive the Aitken-Gaussian extrapolation from the a_4-moment
  # KK-threshold structure at runtime (substrate-first), NOT read the archive
  # text literal. See "Source-Reconciliation note" in the Input-SHA Ledger.
  kk_l5_results:
    path: "computations/session-66/s66_kk_threshold_l5_results.txt"
    sha256: "<computed-at-runtime>"   # archive reference (cross-check only; the value is re-derived substrate-first)

# ---- fb_pair (CROSS-WAVE OUTPUT CONTRACT) ----
fb_pair:
  forward: >
    a_4^{ζ}-tagged KK-threshold moment structure (a_4_FW_zeta=1350.7216, S75);
    s66 Aitken-Gaussian S-series (S_4=1.14290915); m_H_FW_KK_threshold=131.8;
    S101-M0-BCS-SCREENING lineage (audit 1a1eff66, item 19 feeds the residual level);
    HIGGS-ZETA-67 (138.5 excluded)
  backward: >
    Wave-5 CF-S102-BF-SPINE-VS-LCDM (item 23) CONSUMES this verdict via the
    pre-registered 3-state map:
      (a) FORCED + band-HIT (forced route lands within the m_H PDG band) -> BF
          ceiling 31.62 (the m_H per-factor b_mH=1.5 contributes its full weight);
      (b) FORCED + band-MISS (forced route lands OUTSIDE the PDG band) -> BF
          floor ~2 (SCHEME-FLOATING -> STRAINED-PINNED; m_H contributes anecdotal);
      (c) NO-forced-route (FAIL-ACCOMMODATION) -> m_H EXITS the incumbent set
          (m_H is an ACCOMMODATION surface, not a prediction; removed from the
          per-factor BF decomposition).
    The 3 states are FIXED before item 23 runs (anti-post-hoc).

dual_prior:
  track_A: "0.5 — Reading_1 (STRUCTURAL): the a_4-moment KK-series convergence diagnostic FORCES a unique route (a substrate-derived prediction)"
  track_B: "0.5 — Reading_2 (ACCOMMODATION): the diagnostic is inconclusive; the route is selected by proximity to PDG (a best-fit, not a prediction)"
  discriminator: >
    PASS -> 0.9 to Track A (unique route forced, no PDG appeal) -> Wave-5 3-state
    (a) or (b) per band-hit; FAIL-ACCOMMODATION -> 0.9 to Track B -> Wave-5

    borderline; routes to the phonon-first x connes a_4-convergence workshop).
```

## Wave 4 → Wave 5 Decision Point

**Item 20 (`S102-MH-ROUTE-SELECTION`) is the cross-wave output contract.** Its verdict is consumed by Wave-5 item 23 (`CF-S102-BF-SPINE-VS-LCDM`, owner mack-cosmic-bridge) via the pre-registered 3-state map (FIXED before item 23 runs — anti-post-hoc per the BF-spine workshop):

| Item 20 verdict | m_H route outcome | Wave-5 item 23 m_H 3-state | BF_spine consequence |
|:----------------|:------------------|:---------------------------|:---------------------|
| **PASS + band-HIT** | unique route FORCED, lands within m_H PDG band | (a) m_H per-factor b_mH = 1.5 (full weight) | ceiling **31.62** (very-strong, NOT decisive) |
| **PASS + band-MISS** | unique route FORCED, lands OUTSIDE m_H PDG band | (b) SCHEME-FLOATING → STRAINED-PINNED; m_H anecdotal | floor **~2** |
| **FAIL-ACCOMMODATION** | no forced route (proximity-to-PDG only) | (c) m_H EXITS the incumbent set | m_H removed from per-factor BF decomposition |
| **INFO** | a_4-convergence borderline | default b_mH ≤ 1.5 UNCHANGED, pending phonon-first×connes workshop | ceiling 31.62 pending workshop |

Item 19 (`CF-S102-M0-TRANSFER-CONVENTION`) feeds item 20 indirectly: the derived screening transfer level sets the m_H residual magnitude, which sharpens the band-HIT/band-MISS determination in 3-states (a)/(b). Item 19 and item 20 both run in Wave 4 (item 20 does NOT block on item 19 — the route-selection criterion is convergence-based, independent of the screening level; item 19's output refines the band-membership reporting only).

**Items 15–18** produce no cross-wave consumers within S102; their verdicts update the fermion-sector constraint map and feed downstream (next-session) fermion-texture and neutrino-mass-matrix gates per each gate's `fb_pair.backward`.
